cards.front: Which features point to acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL)?
cards.back: Mostly **children**. The marrow is full of **TdT-positive lymphoblasts** (TdT marks immature lymphoid cells). Risk is higher in **Down syndrome**. **t(12;21)** carries a good prognosis. The **CNS** and **testes** are sanctuary sites for relapse.
cards.back_pt: Principalmente **crianças**. A medula está repleta de **linfoblastos TdT-positivos** (a TdT marca células linfoides imaturas). O risco é maior na **síndrome de Down**. A **t(12;21)** tem bom prognóstico. O **SNC** e os **testículos** são santuários de recidiva.

cards.front: Which findings show that the blasts in an acute leukemia are myeloid (AML)?
cards.back: **Myeloblasts** that are **myeloperoxidase (MPO)-positive** and may contain **Auer rods** (red-pink, needle-shaped rods of fused primary granules). AML is mainly a disease of **adults**. **Monocytic** AML can infiltrate the gums (**gingival hyperplasia**) and skin.
cards.back_pt: **Mieloblastos** **positivos para mieloperoxidase (MPO)** que podem conter **bastonetes de Auer** (bastões róseo-avermelhados, em forma de agulha, formados por grânulos primários fundidos). A LMA é sobretudo uma doença de **adultos**. A LMA **monocítica** pode infiltrar a gengiva (**hiperplasia gengival**) e a pele.

cards.front: Why is acute promyelocytic leukemia (APL) an emergency, and what is the treatment concept?
cards.back: **t(15;17)** forms **PML-RARA**, which blocks maturation at the promyelocyte stage. Procoagulant granules trigger **DIC**, so early bleeding can kill. **All-trans retinoic acid (ATRA)** forces the cells to mature; it is often combined with arsenic trioxide.
cards.back_pt: A **t(15;17)** forma **PML-RARA**, que bloqueia a maturação no estágio de promielócito. Grânulos pró-coagulantes desencadeiam **CIVD**, e o sangramento precoce pode matar. O **ácido all-trans-retinoico (ATRA, tretinoína)** força a maturação das células; costuma ser associado ao trióxido de arsênio.

cards.front: What are the key findings in chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL)?
cards.back: Older adults with many **small mature B cells** and **smudge cells** on the smear. Phenotype: **CD5+, CD19+, CD20+ (dim), CD23+**. Complications: **warm autoimmune hemolytic anemia**, infections from low antibodies, and **Richter transformation** to diffuse large B-cell lymphoma.
cards.back_pt: Idosos com muitos **linfócitos B pequenos e maduros** e **sombras de Gumprecht** (*smudge cells*) no esfregaço. Fenótipo: **CD5+, CD19+, CD20+ (fraco), CD23+**. Complicações: **anemia hemolítica autoimune por anticorpos quentes**, infecções por hipogamaglobulinemia e **transformação de Richter** em linfoma difuso de grandes células B.

cards.front: Which findings suggest hairy cell leukemia?
cards.back: A middle-aged man with **massive splenomegaly** and **pancytopenia** (with very low monocytes), usually without lymphadenopathy. B cells with hairlike projections are **TRAP-positive**. Marrow fibrosis gives a **dry tap**. Most cases carry the **BRAF V600E** mutation.
cards.back_pt: Homem de meia-idade com **esplenomegalia volumosa** e **pancitopenia** (com monocitopenia acentuada), em geral sem linfadenopatia. Linfócitos B com projeções pilosas são **TRAP-positivos**. A fibrose medular causa **aspirado seco** (*dry tap*). A maioria dos casos tem a mutação **BRAF V600E**.

cards.front: How do the subtypes of classical Hodgkin lymphoma differ?
cards.back: **Nodular sclerosis**: most common; collagen bands, **lacunar cells**, mediastinal mass in young adults. **Mixed cellularity**: often **EBV**-positive, many eosinophils. **Lymphocyte-rich**: best prognosis. **Lymphocyte-depleted**: worst prognosis; older or HIV-positive patients.
cards.back_pt: **Esclerose nodular**: a mais comum; faixas de colágeno, **células lacunares**, massa mediastinal em adultos jovens. **Celularidade mista**: frequentemente **EBV**-positiva, muitos eosinófilos. **Rico em linfócitos**: melhor prognóstico. **Depleção linfocitária**: pior prognóstico; idosos ou pessoas com HIV.

cards.front: Which translocation and gene define follicular, Burkitt and mantle cell lymphoma?
cards.back: **Follicular**: **t(14;18)**, BCL2 overexpression blocks apoptosis; indolent. **Burkitt**: **t(8;14)**, MYC drives very fast growth; *starry sky* pattern. **Mantle cell**: **t(11;14)**, **cyclin D1** overexpression; CD5-positive.
cards.back_pt: **Folicular**: **t(14;18)**, a hiperexpressão de BCL2 bloqueia a apoptose; indolente. **Burkitt**: **t(8;14)**, o MYC impulsiona crescimento muito rápido; padrão em *céu estrelado* (*starry sky*). **Células do manto**: **t(11;14)**, hiperexpressão de **ciclina D1**; CD5-positivo.

cards.front: Which lab changes define tumor lysis syndrome?
cards.back: Dying tumor cells release their contents: **hyperkalemia**, **hyperphosphatemia**, **hyperuricemia** and **hypocalcemia** (phosphate binds calcium). Uric acid and calcium phosphate crystals cause **acute kidney injury**. Classic after starting therapy for **Burkitt lymphoma** or high-count **ALL**.
cards.back_pt: As células tumorais que morrem liberam seu conteúdo: **hipercalemia**, **hiperfosfatemia**, **hiperuricemia** e **hipocalcemia** (o fosfato se liga ao cálcio). Cristais de ácido úrico e de fosfato de cálcio causam **lesão renal aguda**. Típica ao iniciar o tratamento de **linfoma de Burkitt** ou de **LLA** com leucometria alta.

questions.stem: A 50-year-old man has 3 months of fatigue and a feeling of fullness in the left upper abdomen. The spleen is palpable 10 cm below the costal margin. There is no lymphadenopathy. Hemoglobin is 9.1 g/dL, leukocyte count is 2,100/mm3, and platelet count is 68,000/mm3. The blood smear shows a few medium-sized lymphocytes with fine hairlike cytoplasmic projections. Bone marrow aspiration yields no material, and the biopsy shows reticulin fibrosis. Flow cytometry shows clonal B cells that express CD11c, CD25 and CD103. Which molecular change is most likely present in these cells?
questions.explanation: Pancytopenia, massive splenomegaly, a **dry tap** and clonal B cells with hairlike projections that express CD11c, CD25 and CD103 indicate **hairy cell leukemia** (the cells are also **TRAP-positive**), which almost always carries **BRAF V600E**. JAK2 V617F is tempting because primary myelofibrosis also gives a dry tap and a big spleen, but it is a myeloid neoplasm with teardrop cells, not a clonal B-cell disease.
questions.explanation_pt: Pancitopenia, esplenomegalia volumosa, **aspirado seco** e linfócitos B clonais com projeções pilosas que expressam CD11c, CD25 e CD103 indicam **tricoleucemia** (leucemia de células pilosas; as células também são **TRAP-positivas**), que quase sempre tem **BRAF V600E**. A JAK2 V617F é tentadora porque a mielofibrose primária também causa aspirado seco e baço grande, mas é uma neoplasia mieloide com dacriócitos, e não uma doença clonal de linfócitos B.

questions.stem: A 66-year-old man has 3 months of fatigue, night sweats and a 5-kg weight loss. He has painless enlarged lymph nodes in the neck, axillae and groin, and the spleen is palpable 4 cm below the costal margin. Colonoscopy, done for occult blood in the stool, shows many small polyps throughout the colon. Lymph node biopsy shows a diffuse growth of small to medium-sized lymphocytes with irregular nuclei. Flow cytometry shows clonal B cells that are CD5-positive, CD20-positive and CD23-negative. Which chromosomal translocation is most likely present?
questions.explanation: This is **mantle cell lymphoma**: an older man with widespread nodes, spleen and bowel involvement (*lymphomatous polyposis*), and small B cells that are **CD5-positive but CD23-negative**. **t(11;14)** places the **cyclin D1** gene next to the immunoglobulin heavy chain gene, so the cells pass the G1/S checkpoint too easily. t(14;18) is tempting because follicular lymphoma also has small cleaved cells, but its cells are CD5-negative and form follicles. CLL is also CD5-positive, but it is CD23-positive.
questions.explanation_pt: Trata-se de **linfoma de células do manto**: homem mais velho com linfonodos disseminados, acometimento do baço e do intestino (*polipose linfomatosa*) e linfócitos B pequenos **CD5-positivos, mas CD23-negativos**. A **t(11;14)** coloca o gene da **ciclina D1** ao lado do gene da cadeia pesada de imunoglobulina, e as células passam com facilidade demais pelo ponto de checagem G1/S. A t(14;18) é tentadora porque o linfoma folicular também tem células pequenas clivadas, mas suas células são CD5-negativas e formam folículos. A LLC também é CD5-positiva, mas é CD23-positiva.

questions.stem: A 24-year-old woman has 2 months of fevers, drenching night sweats and a 6-kg weight loss. She has a painless, firm, rubbery 3-cm lymph node above the left clavicle. Chest x-ray shows a widened mediastinum. Lymph node biopsy shows thick bands of collagen that divide the node into nodules. Within the nodules there are large cells that sit in clear spaces, plus scattered large binucleate cells with prominent nucleoli. These large cells are positive for CD15 and CD30. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: **CD15+/CD30+ Reed-Sternberg cells** mean **classical Hodgkin lymphoma**, and B symptoms with a mediastinal mass in a young woman fit. **Collagen bands** and **lacunar cells** (cells in clear spaces) define **nodular sclerosis**, the most common subtype. Mixed cellularity also has Reed-Sternberg cells, but it lacks fibrous bands and shows many eosinophils and often EBV. T-lymphoblastic lymphoma causes a mediastinal mass in teenagers, but its cells are TdT-positive blasts.
questions.explanation_pt: **Células de Reed-Sternberg CD15+/CD30+** indicam **linfoma de Hodgkin clássico**, e sintomas B com massa mediastinal em mulher jovem são compatíveis. **Faixas de colágeno** e **células lacunares** (células em espaços claros) definem a **esclerose nodular**, o subtipo mais comum. A celularidade mista também tem células de Reed-Sternberg, mas não tem faixas fibrosas e mostra muitos eosinófilos e frequentemente EBV. O linfoma linfoblástico T causa massa mediastinal em adolescentes, mas suas células são blastos TdT-positivos.

questions.stem: A 34-year-old man comes to the emergency department with bleeding gums and large bruises on his arms for 4 days. Hemoglobin is 8.2 g/dL, leukocyte count is 1,800/mm3, and platelet count is 19,000/mm3. Prothrombin time is prolonged, fibrinogen is low, and D-dimer is markedly elevated. The blood smear shows abnormal promyelocytes with dense granules and bundles of Auer rods. Bone marrow cytogenetics shows t(15;17). Which mechanism best describes the main targeted drug used first for this leukemia?
choices: Inhibition of the BCR-ABL tyrosine kinase
Induction of maturation of the leukemic cells into granulocytes
questions.explanation: This is **acute promyelocytic leukemia** with **DIC**. The **PML-RARA** fusion blocks retinoic acid signaling and arrests the cells at the promyelocyte stage. **ATRA** overcomes this block and makes the cells **mature** into granulocytes, which also helps control the coagulopathy. Imatinib inhibits BCR-ABL from t(9;22), the fusion of CML, and has no role against PML-RARA.
questions.explanation_pt: Trata-se de **leucemia promielocítica aguda** com **CIVD**. A fusão **PML-RARA** bloqueia a sinalização do ácido retinoico e interrompe a maturação das células no estágio de promielócito. O **ATRA** supera esse bloqueio e faz as células **amadurecerem** em granulócitos, o que também ajuda a controlar a coagulopatia. O imatinibe inibe o BCR-ABL da t(9;22), a fusão da LMC, e não tem papel contra o PML-RARA.

notes.title: Leukemias and lymphomas: types, markers and complications
notes.body_md:
## Acute leukemias

- Blasts fill the marrow: **pancytopenia** (fatigue, infections, bleeding) and **bone pain**.
- **ALL**: children; **TdT+** lymphoblasts; linked to **Down syndrome**; **t(12;21)** has a good prognosis; relapse in the **CNS** and **testes**.
- **AML**: adults; **MPO+** myeloblasts with **Auer rods**. **APL** (t(15;17)): **DIC**, treated with **ATRA**. **Monocytic** AML: gum infiltration.

## Chronic leukemias

- **CLL**: older adults; small mature B cells, **smudge cells**; CD5+, CD23+; warm hemolysis; **Richter transformation**.
- **Hairy cell leukemia**: **TRAP+**, **dry tap**, big spleen, **BRAF V600E**.
- **CML**: see the myeloproliferative block.

## Hodgkin lymphoma

- **Reed-Sternberg cells** (CD15+, CD30+) in a reactive background.
- **Bimodal** age; often **cervical** or mediastinal nodes; spreads to **contiguous** node groups.
- **B symptoms**: fever, night sweats, weight loss. **Pel-Ebstein fever** comes and goes over weeks.
- **Nodular sclerosis** (most common, lacunar cells), **mixed cellularity** (EBV), lymphocyte-rich (best), lymphocyte-depleted (worst).

## Non-Hodgkin lymphoma

- Often noncontiguous and extranodal spread.
- **Diffuse large B-cell**: most common, aggressive.
- **Follicular**: t(14;18), BCL2; indolent; centrocytes and centroblasts.
- **Burkitt**: t(8;14), MYC; *starry sky*; **EBV** in the endemic African jaw form.
- **Mantle cell**: t(11;14), cyclin D1; CD5+.
- **Marginal zone (MALT)**: chronic inflammation from **H. pylori**, **Sjögren** or **Hashimoto**.
- **Adult T-cell leukemia/lymphoma**: **HTLV-1**; Japan, Caribbean, parts of Africa and Brazil; hypercalcemia.
- **Mycosis fungoides**: skin CD4+ T cells, **Pautrier microabscesses**; **Sézary syndrome** is its leukemic form.

## Other topics

- **Langerhans cell histiocytosis**: **S-100+**, **CD1a+**, **Birbeck granules** (tennis racket); lytic bone lesions in children.
- **Ann Arbor staging**: I, one node region; II, two or more on one side of the diaphragm; III, both sides; IV, diffuse spread to organs outside the lymph system (for example liver or bone marrow). B = B symptoms.
- **Tumor lysis syndrome**: high potassium, phosphate and uric acid; low calcium; AKI (see the renal blocks).
- Chemotherapy drugs: see the pharmacology block.

## Markers

- **CD19/CD20**: B cells. **CD3**: T cells. **CD34**: stem cells and blasts. **CD15/CD30**: Reed-Sternberg cells. **CD5**: T cells, plus CLL and mantle cell lymphoma.
notes.body_pt_md:
## Leucemias agudas

- Blastos ocupam a medula: **pancitopenia** (fadiga, infecções, sangramento) e **dor óssea**.
- **LLA**: crianças; linfoblastos **TdT+**; associada à **síndrome de Down**; **t(12;21)** tem bom prognóstico; recidiva no **SNC** e nos **testículos**.
- **LMA**: adultos; mieloblastos **MPO+** com **bastonetes de Auer**. **LPA** (t(15;17)): **CIVD**, tratada com **ATRA**. LMA **monocítica**: infiltração gengival.

## Leucemias crônicas

- **LLC**: idosos; linfócitos B pequenos e maduros, **sombras de Gumprecht**; CD5+, CD23+; hemólise por anticorpos quentes; **transformação de Richter**.
- **Tricoleucemia**: **TRAP+**, **aspirado seco**, baço grande, **BRAF V600E**.
- **LMC**: ver o bloco de neoplasias mieloproliferativas.

## Linfoma de Hodgkin

- **Células de Reed-Sternberg** (CD15+, CD30+) em meio reativo.
- Idade **bimodal**; frequentemente linfonodos **cervicais** ou mediastinais; disseminação para grupos linfonodais **contíguos**.
- **Sintomas B**: febre, sudorese noturna, perda de peso. A **febre de Pel-Ebstein** vai e volta ao longo de semanas.
- **Esclerose nodular** (mais comum, células lacunares), **celularidade mista** (EBV), rico em linfócitos (melhor), depleção linfocitária (pior).

## Linfoma não Hodgkin

- Disseminação frequentemente não contígua e extranodal.
- **Difuso de grandes células B**: o mais comum, agressivo.
- **Folicular**: t(14;18), BCL2; indolente; centrócitos e centroblastos.
- **Burkitt**: t(8;14), MYC; *céu estrelado*; **EBV** na forma endêmica africana de mandíbula.
- **Células do manto**: t(11;14), ciclina D1; CD5+.
- **Zona marginal (MALT)**: inflamação crônica por **H. pylori**, **Sjögren** ou **Hashimoto**.
- **Leucemia/linfoma de células T do adulto**: **HTLV-1**; Japão, Caribe, partes da África e Brasil; hipercalcemia.
- **Micose fungoide**: linfócitos T CD4+ na pele, **microabscessos de Pautrier**; a **síndrome de Sézary** é sua forma leucêmica.

## Outros tópicos

- **Histiocitose de células de Langerhans**: **S-100+**, **CD1a+**, **grânulos de Birbeck** (em raquete de tênis); lesões ósseas líticas em crianças.
- **Estadiamento de Ann Arbor**: I, uma região linfonodal; II, duas ou mais do mesmo lado do diafragma; III, ambos os lados; IV, disseminação difusa para órgãos fora do sistema linfático (por exemplo, fígado ou medula óssea). B = sintomas B.
- **Síndrome de lise tumoral**: potássio, fosfato e ácido úrico altos; cálcio baixo; LRA (ver os blocos renais).
- Quimioterápicos: ver o bloco de farmacologia.

## Marcadores

- **CD19/CD20**: linfócitos B. **CD3**: linfócitos T. **CD34**: células-tronco e blastos. **CD15/CD30**: células de Reed-Sternberg. **CD5**: linfócitos T, além de LLC e linfoma de células do manto.
